purpose: Non-windowed verification of Rust folder create/rename form state, validation, layout and static scene text; modal/Metal/persistence runtime acceptance deferred
build_consistency: final Ninja dry run reported no work to do
unit_verified_mechanisms: Rust owns create/root/subfolder/rename copy, Unicode whitespace trimming, empty-name and existing 256-byte UTF-8 validation. Tests cover Polish/Japanese/emoji, exactly 256 versus 258 UTF-8 bytes, whitespace-only input and retaining zero-width space as Chromium does.
Submission rechecks source workspace, readiness/busy state and live folder/parent IDs. Pins cannot act as folders. Composition, duplicate, cancelled and already accepted submissions return no action.
Immediate rejection can retry with the same name; accepted admission closes controller state. This is not confirmation of durable asynchronous storage.
Rust lays out label, minimum-height native editor and optional error without overlapping. Zero/narrow/font-height/saturated dimensions remain bounded. Static form text uses the Rust display list.
implemented_pending_runtime_verification: The opt-in modal uses a custom FolderFormView in the existing DialogModel host. The body creates a native Textfield and static-text AX Views without hidden Labels; Rust supplies title/field/button copy and body layout.

Two small shared-context Metal canvases draw only label/error regions and exclude the native editor. Native fallback consumes the same Rust scene recipe. Native modal title/buttons, initial focus, Enter/Escape, clipboard and IME remain adapters.

The accept adapter reads current native text, prevents acceptance during IME composition, obtains a typed Rust request and calls existing create/rename application services. A temporarily expanded parent is restored on immediate application rejection.

Accepted application admission closes the form. Existing configuration writes, asynchronous rollback and separate ShowFolderSaveError presentation remain unchanged; delete confirmation and save-error dialogs are not migrated here.

Error changes update AX names/visibility, request a native alert event and resize through the modal host. Caret-only invalidations skip scene scheduling; unchanged error text does not resize/redraw. Surface teardown follows the custom View lifecycle.

The compiled GUI regression checks no Labels in the custom body, scene text, editor/non-text bounds, empty/long validation, IME composition, Unicode create/rename, removed parent and changed workspace. It has not been executed.
deferred_checkpoint: Run the curated 47-case Metal matrix (prior 46 plus FolderFormScenesValidationCompositionAndStaleContext).

Expand Views controls from 17 to 20 by adding SidebarFoldersCreateNestAndPersist, SidebarFolderRenameAndDeleteContents and SidebarFolderFailedWriteRollsBack; run all three folder cases in both backends.
Verify actual modal focus/selection/Enter/Escape/IME and alert announcements, static canvas clipping, missing-drawable fallback/recovery, sizing/theme/scale and dialog teardown.
Verify parent expansion and immediate rejection rollback, accepted async configuration writes, failed-write rollback/save-error dialog, cancellation/stale contexts and profile/session isolation.
Package/sign and inspect the matching isolated app. Measure actual CPU/GPU/presentation workload separately; test durations and submitted command buffers are not performance gains.
limitations: Compilation and non-windowed unit tests do not establish native modal/Metal/IME/AX behavior, persistence integration, visual quality or speedup. Those remain unaccepted until the GUI checkpoint.
Modal host/title/button presentation, native editing/focus/IME, delete confirmation and asynchronous-error dialogs still use native adapters/Views. Full UI migration is incomplete.
Domain validation, persistence, filesystem failures and rollback remain application services. This form acknowledges admission and does not claim storage success.
No dependency, crate or framework was added; original-code Apache-2.0 and required upstream notices are unchanged.
